authorityBoundary.note: date-only calendar conversion evidence does not authorize 子時, 야자시/day boundary, true-solar-time, or other Saju semantic policy changes

implementation.baseCalculation: Date.UTC(1900, 1, 30) plus (offset + day - 31) yields lunar 1900-01-01 at solar 1900-01-31; no overflow occurs for the lower boundary
implementation.productionChange: remove only the 1900 lunar lower-bound clause from lunar2solar
implementation.unsupportedRangePolicy: return -1 outside the table-backed solar interval 1900-01-31 through 2100-12-31; do not extrapolate into 1899 or 2101

rootCause.coordinateError: 31 is the Gregorian solar anchor day, not a lunar month-1 day limit; lunar 1900-01-01 is the first supported lunar input and lunar month 1 has 29 days
rootCause.guardOriginEvidence: the copied solarlunar family uses the same parameter-range condition and labels it as the maximum boundary; its 1900 lower-bound clause is valid for solar2lunar but misapplied when copied into lunar2solar
rootCause.historyFinding: lunarConverter.js was introduced in that commit; git history has no earlier implementation or narrower rationale for the condition
rootCause.why28: the immutable KASI v1 capture contains lunar 1900-01-02 through 1900-01-29, mapping to solar 1900-02-01 through 1900-02-28; every one was rejected before calculation

solarRange.lowerBoundMeaning: solar2lunar accepts the first solar date whose lunar table anchor is lunar 1900-01-01; lunar2solar accepts that lunar anchor directly
solarRange.upperBoundMeaning: the table has lunar year 2100, but only lunar 2100-12-01 maps inside the solar 2100 maximum; later lunar dates would overflow into 2101

title: KASI lunar2solar 1900 lower-bound mismatch root cause and implementation fix
